newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge says earnings fell in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge says earnings fell in quarter.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp. said Thursday its earnings slumped in the latest quarter, blaming the downturn on lower copper prices.
The world's largest copper producer said it earned $88.2 million, or $1.22 a share, in the third quarter, versus year-ago profits of $211.9 million, or $3.03 a share.
Revenues fell to $853.70 million from $1.07 billion.

Phelps Dodge said the drop in earnings resulted mainly from lower copper prices, noting that the price of copper on New York's Commodity Exchange averaged 91 cents a pound in the third quarter, compared with an average of $1.36 last year. In the first nine months of 1996, copper prices have averaged $1.08 a pound.
The company's copper production rose to 187,900 tons from 182,300 tons in last year's third quarter and copper sales slipped to 194,500 tons from 196,600 tons.
Despite the weaker results, Phelps Dodge's stock gained $1.125 to $63.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
